A1.justification: Both PDFs describe L2RSI, with matching core text, datasets and benchmark tables. However, v2 explicitly identifies itself as an extract: its Methodology section is a stub with unresolved references, and substantial method and supplementary material is unavailable. Both supplied PDFs are readable, but these omissions limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original L2RSI and baseline retrieval results on XA-L&RSI and Oxford-L&RSI in Table 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, ablations and robustness experiments, including KITTI360-L&RSI results in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The shared text retains semantic contrastive alignment and STPE particle aggregation. However, v2 omits detailed methodology, preventing comparison of v3's encoder architecture, loss, segmentation pipeline and particle-propagation procedure. These cannot reliably be classified as new method components.

E1.justification: XA-L&RSI and Oxford-L&RSI coverage is retained. v3 also reports KITTI360-L&RSI evaluation, SemanticKITTI segmentation training and motion-noise scenarios. Missing methodology and supplementary material in v2 prevent establishing whether these represent expanded coverage.

E2.justification: The matched Table 3 adds LIP-Loc across all six XA-L&RSI and Oxford-L&RSI evaluation columns. GeoDTR, Sample4Geo, FRGeo, SuperGlobal and particle-filtering comparisons remain, establishing a limited comparator expansion.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.1 specifies 40 m spacing and one-third overlap for 60 m remote-sensing submaps; v3 Section 5.1 specifies 20 m and two-thirds overlap. Table 2 counts and the 30 m correctness threshold remain unchanged. This is a reported preprocessing revision, without establishing reruns. v3 also specifies BEV input for the added LIP-Loc comparison.

E4.justification: Both Table 3s already compare STPE with no refinement, SuperGlobal and particle filtering. v3 additionally presents component and parameter ablations, motion-noise tests, encoder and compatibility analyses, and qualitative failures. The corresponding detailed experimental and appendix material is unavailable in v2, so these cannot reliably be identified as additions.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.3.3 reports averages over three repeated motion-noise experiments, but their earlier counterpart is unavailable. Whether repeated-run information or averaging was newly introduced is therefore unresolved. The matched main benchmark tables both report point estimates without uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: In the matched Table 3, L2RSI without STPE on Test Set-G changes from 22.62/60.32 to 20.07/52.55 Recall@1/Recall@10, and LIP-Loc results are added. Full L2RSI remains at 83.27/87.82 there; other retained entries are unchanged. The reported spacing revision prevents interpreting the changed values as a demonstrated same-setting performance loss.

T1.justification: The shared retrieval definition in Equation 1 is unchanged. v3 provides the contrastive objective and detailed STPE equations, including particle transitions and Gaussian-mixture assumptions, but v2's detailed method is unavailable. Additions or revisions to this mathematical content cannot be established.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: large-scale cross-view LiDAR localization through semantic alignment and STPE, 83.27% top-1 recall within 30 m over 100 km², and cross-scene generalization without fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Matched result interpretations and magnetometer-related future work remain unchanged. v3 discusses rural semantic sparsity, vegetation and LiDAR field-of-view mismatch, encoder behavior, and temporal-change failures. Missing v2 supplementary discussion prevents determining which explanations and limitations are new.

D1.justification: The matched implementation paragraph expands from v2 Section 4.3 to v3 Appendix A.2: it now specifies 100 epochs, learning rate 5×10^-5, batch size 64, and StepLR decay of 0.95 every 1000 steps. Adam and hardware remain unchanged. These are additional documented settings, not evidence of changed training.

R1.justification: The corresponding evaluation discussion adds a LIP-Loc citation and explicitly includes cross-modal 3D methods alongside cross-view 2D methods, modestly broadening the comparison positioning. The much broader related-work section in v3 cannot be treated as wholly new because v2 is an extract.

P1.justification: Visible edits include author and affiliation changes, a rewritten methodology overview, revised baseline-description wording, and relocation of implementation details to Appendix A.2. The shared abstract, introduction and conclusion remain largely verbatim. Missing v2 sections prevent attributing the wider structural expansion to revision alone.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column conference layout, substantially altering text and figure placement. Figure 1 replaces its abstract semantic-space graphic with segmented examples, and Tables 1 and 2 are restructured. The dataset visualization is retained as Figure 3 rather than Figure 2. These are substantial visible presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The added LIP-Loc comparison and more explicit training settings provide identifiable benefits while headline results remain unchanged. However, v2's missing method and supplementary material prevent establishing how much of v3's apparent additional validation and explanation is new. The unexplained spacing revision alongside unchanged database counts adds uncertainty, so a reliable paper-level net improvement cannot be determined.
